evidence: Confirmed closure implies adequate reviewed evidence, which implies execution and a credible planned path; converses do not follow.
Confirmed compound requirements require all subclaims plus applicable integration conditions.
Confirmed child closure implies parent closure only under complete allocation and a justified composition argument.
Confirmed traceability proves relationships, not semantic correctness or evidence sufficiency.
Confirmed waiver can close an action without making technical satisfaction true.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Logical structures bound claims but do not assert that any arbitrary requirement graph is complete or correct.

evidence: Challenged compound, ambiguous, statistical, inherited, derived, interface, parent/child, process, hazard, and cross-cutting requirements.
Reviewed proxies, post hoc criteria, obsolete baselines, missing conditions, wrong levels, configuration mismatch, and source drift.
Reviewed many-to-many activities/evidence, summary reports, raw provenance, contradictory results, open anomalies, waiver, and invalid runs.
Reviewed supplier/heritage evidence, continuous builds, dependencies, automation, flaky/quarantined tests, and evidence credit.
Reviewed misleading aggregate coverage, criticality, omitted applicable rows, orphan activities/evidence, and dangling superseded links.

boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real closure requires relevant stakeholder, requirements, architecture, integration, test/analysis, metrology/statistics, supplier, human-factors, safety/security, configuration/data/quality, independent V&V, technical authority, acceptance, and certification expertise.

evidence: Confirmed every applicable requirement has stable identity, source, baseline, applicability, owner, and verification path.
Confirmed semantic agreement among requirement, oracle, method, level, article, conditions, procedure, and evidence.
Confirmed evidence identity includes product and all relevant procedure/tool/model/data/instrument/environment versions.
Confirmed technical statuses remain distinct and anomalies/negative evidence remain linked through correction and retest.
Confirmed critical closure cannot be hidden by aggregate percentages or administrative waiver.
Confirmed bidirectional change impact governs re-verification and reuse.
invariant_checking.notes: No trace link, method letter, test campaign pass, child pass, supplier certificate, waiver, percentage, or automated result is presented as sufficient closure by itself.

proof_review.notes: The chapter presents implication and composition reasoning but no theorem proof.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked requirement-based verification, verification statements, bidirectional trace, matrix/evidence graph, applicability, success criteria, objective evidence, closure package, coverage, status, and composition.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked authoritative baselines, requirement validation/parsing, compound and hierarchical claims, methods/levels, implementation versus evidence, provenance, anomalies/waivers, closure, metrics, reuse, automation, and change impact.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from requirement identity to closure and lifecycle evidence governance. Ten distinct examples and five complete solutions cover specification defects, shared tests, hierarchy, suppliers, anomalies, baseline change, statistics, safety, continuous delivery, and metrics.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external NASA/FAA expert, regulator, customer/stakeholder, requirements owner, architecture/integration/test engineer, statistician/metrologist, supplier, human-factors specialist, safety/security engineer, configuration/data/quality authority, independent V&V reviewer, technical authority, acceptance authority, or certification body review is claimed.
